sections.title: Suicide screen (C-SSRS screener)
sections.alert: Yes to question 4 or 5, or suicidal behaviour in the past 3 months: do not leave the patient alone, remove means, and arrange same-day psychiatric assessment. Complete the risk assessment below; the screener supports clinical judgement and does not replace it (NICE NG225).

fields.label: 1. Wished to be dead, or to go to sleep and not wake up (past month)
2. Actual thoughts of killing yourself (past month)
fields.hint: if no, go straight to question 6

fields.label: 3. Thought about how you might do this (past month)
4. Had these thoughts with some intention of acting on them (past month)
fields.hint: as opposed to: I have the thoughts but I definitely will not do anything about them

fields.label: 5. Started to work out or worked out the details of how to kill yourself, and intend to carry out this plan (past month)
6. Ever done anything, started to do anything, or prepared to do anything to end your life
fields.hint: e.g. collected tablets, wrote a will or suicide note, gave away valuables, or an actual attempt

fields.label: Yes to question 4 or 5, or suicidal behaviour in the past 3 months

sections.title: Risk assessment
sections.alert: Follow the self-harm and suicide risk protocol. If suicidal intent is high, do not leave the patient unsupervised: keep them with staff in a safe area, remove means, and arrange urgent psychiatric assessment. Act on safeguarding concerns under local procedures.

fields.label: Access to means (pesticides, medicines, ropes, weapons)
Self-harm or suicide attempt in this episode
fields.hint: MHCA 2017 section 115: presume severe stress; provide care, not punishment

fields.label: Thoughts, threats or acts of harm to others
Command hallucinations to harm self or others
Safeguarding concern (abuse, violence, exploitation or neglect)
Risk formulation
fields.hint: current dangers, what could change them, protective factors and reasons for living; avoid low, medium or high labels (NICE NG225)

fields.label: Safety plan
opts: Agreed and shared with family (with consent)

fields.label: Capacity for mental healthcare and treatment decisions (section 4)
opts: Needs very high support from nominated representative

fields.label: Capacity findings
fields.hint: can the person understand the relevant information, appreciate the foreseeable consequences, and communicate the decision (section 4(1))

fields.label: Advance directive (section 5)
fields.hint: ask the patient and family; Boards keep an online register (section 7)

fields.label: Nominated representative basis (sections 14 and 15)
opts: Appointed in writing by the patient
Appointed by the Mental Health Review Board

fields.label: Informed consent for treatment given by
opts: Patient with support of nominated representative

fields.label: Right to information given (section 22)
fields.hint: provision and criteria for admission, right to apply to the Board for review, nature of illness, treatment and side effects, in a language the person understands

fields.label: Report to Mental Health Review Board
fields.hint: minor admitted: within 72 hours (section 87(9)); supported admission: within 3 days for a woman or minor, 7 days for others (section 89(9))

sections.title: Fever and rigidity on psychotropics: NMS or serotonin syndrome
sections.alert: Possible NMS or serotonin syndrome: both can be fatal. Stop the suspected drug, check temperature, CK, creatinine and electrolytes, and escalate early. Do not give more antipsychotic to a febrile, rigid, confused patient. Follow the neuroleptic malignant syndrome or serotonin syndrome protocol.

fields.label: Drug exposure
opts: Antipsychotic or other dopamine antagonist started or increased (favours NMS)
Levodopa or other dopaminergic drug stopped (favours NMS)
Serotonergic drug started, increased, combined or taken in overdose (favours serotonin syndrome)

fields.label: Onset after the drug change
opts: Within 24 hours, often within hours (favours serotonin syndrome)
Over 1 to 3 days, usually within 2 weeks of the change (favours NMS)

fields.label: Bradykinesia with normal or reduced reflexes (favours NMS)
Clonus: spontaneous, inducible or ocular (favours serotonin syndrome)
Hyperreflexia and tremor, more marked in the legs (favours serotonin syndrome)
Diarrhoea or hyperactive bowel sounds (favours serotonin syndrome)
Autonomic instability: tachycardia, labile BP, sweating (either)
Altered mental state: agitation, confusion, stupor or mutism (either)
Creatine kinase
fields.hint: raised in NMS, often markedly; can also rise in severe serotonin syndrome

fields.label: Hunter criteria for serotonin toxicity
fields.hint: use the Hunter serotonin toxicity calculator

fields.label: Working diagnosis
opts: Unclear: treat supportively and monitor for both
fields.hint: exclude sepsis, meningitis or encephalitis, heat stroke, anticholinergic toxicity, malignant catatonia, and alcohol or sedative withdrawal

advice.title: Help in a crisis
advice.text: If you have thoughts of harming yourself or ending your life, tell someone you trust and get help straight away: go to the nearest hospital emergency department, or call Tele MANAS on 14416 or 1800-89-14416 (free, 24 hours a day). Keep your safety plan and these numbers with you.

advice.title: Keeping the home safe
advice.text: Ask a family member to lock away all medicines, pesticides, acids and other poisons, and to remove anything else you might use to harm yourself. Share your safety plan with them so they know your warning signs and whom to call.

advice.title: Taking antidepressants
advice.text: Antidepressants usually take 1 to 2 weeks to start working and up to 6 weeks for the full effect, so take them every day even if you notice no change at first. Do not stop them suddenly, and do not take extra to make up for a missed dose. Carry on for as long as your doctor advises, usually at least six months after you feel better. Tell your doctor straight away about troublesome side effects or any thoughts of harming yourself, and ask before drinking alcohol or driving.
